title: Live-check that Codex honors the thread-level tool_timeout_sec TermAl sets for the delegation MCP server
outcome: Raised by the Kimi /review-code child in the w-33bee3bec3f0 review round 5 (delegation-38e5e05d-7430-44e5-a389-29de15d78100, session-8481). w-33bee3bec3f0 writes tool_timeout_sec (about 226 s) into the termal-delegation entry of the Codex thread config (thread/start and resume `config.mcp_servers`). The installed codex-cli 0.157.1 binary has tool_timeout_sec in its MCP server config struct (checked by string search). Whether Codex honors it in thread-level overrides, not only in config.toml, has not been seen live: the Codex quota is exhausted until 2026-10-03. If it is ignored, behavior falls back to Codex's 60 s default, the pre-change behavior. If a Codex build validated unknown keys strictly, thread start would fail. That is unlikely given the struct field.
acceptance: A live Codex session started by TermAl on the installed Codex build shows a delegation tool call (for example source-root naming under a slow capture, or a review-freeze check) outlasting 60 s without Codex ending it, or the thread start is shown to reject the key and TermAl stops sending it
